excerpt_i18n.en: In the past period, the most impressive AI-generated videos often lasted only a few seconds. With natural character states, well-crafted lighting and atmosphere, and sufficiently smooth movements, it was easy to feel that video generation was close to being truly usable. However, as the industry advances, the problems become clearer. The real challenge has never been creating a short, beautiful clip, but maintaining that quality consistently over time. Once the video length is extended, many models begin to gradually destabilize—characters, scenes, and actions may appear to continue, but internal detail drift and temporal looseness emerge. This is why the current bottleneck in the AI video industry is no longer just about generating clips, but about generating continuous, stable content that can sustain a complete context. For example, in a kitchen video, as the camera moves from prepping ingredients to cooking and then to plating, viewers expect the same space, the same set of utensils, and the same ingredients to be naturally connected. Similarly, in a city commute video, as a character walks from a subway exit to a street-side shop, the camera may change, but the character's state, environmental relationships, and action logic must not drift apart. Only by solving this long-term stability issue can AI video truly transition from demonstration to creation and production. It is against this backdrop that Zhang Chi's team at Westlake University proposed "Free-Lunch Long Video Generation via Layer-Adaptive O.O.D Correction."
excerpt_i18n.es: Durante un tiempo, lo más impresionante de los videos generados por IA solían ser los primeros segundos. Pero cuanto más avanza la industria, más claros se vuelven los problemas: lo realmente difícil nunca ha sido crear un fragmento visual bonito, sino mantener esa calidad de manera estable a lo largo del tiempo. items.title: 西湖大学张驰团队：从视觉合成到空间理解，视频 AI 正在「转向」丨CVPR 2026
items.raw_excerpt: 过去两年，视频生成的发展几乎是指数级的。从最早只能生成模糊片段，到如今可以生成具有叙事结构、光影一致性甚至风格控制的长视频，行业表面上已经接近一个阶段性成熟。 但如果把评价标准从“能不能生成一段视频”稍微提高到“能不能控制镜头”，问题就会完全暴露出来。当前大多数模型仍然停留在一种近似二维的生成范式中，它们擅长在时间上延续视觉模式，却缺乏对空间结构的稳定建模能力。 一旦涉及视角变化，模型往往无法保证同一个物体在不同帧之间的几何一致性，人物会发生细微但累积的漂移，建筑结构在移动中逐渐扭曲，遮挡关系也难以维持连续，这意味着模型生成的并不是一个被持续观察的世界，而是一系列在视觉上相似但空间上不一致的结果。 在这样的行业背景下，西湖大学 AGI Lab 研究团队提出了论文《Taming Video Models for 3D and 4D Generation via Zero Shot Camera Control》，值得一提的是，这篇论文也入选了 CVPR Highlight。与以往通过重新训练模型来引入控制能力的路径不同，这项工作将问题重新落回到推理阶段本身，尝试在不改变模型参数的情况下，让相机轨迹成为生成过程中的约束条件，使模型在每一步生成中持续对齐同一个空间结构。 换句话说，这项研究关注的不是如何让模型生成更多内容，而是如何让模型在视角变化中保持世界的一致性，从而把视频生成从二维视觉合成，推进到具有三维结构约束的动态世界建模。 如果从应用角度理解这一点，可以把它看成一种能力的转变。过去模型更像一个能够不断画出新画面的系统，而现在的目标，是让模型像一个可以移动的摄影机，在同一个场景中进行观察和记录。无论是商品展示、空间漫游，还是内容创作中的镜头设计，本质上都依赖这种能力的成立。 WorldForge 的提出，正是在这一关键转折点上，给出了一个不依赖额外训练、却能够实现精确相机

excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past two years, video generation has advanced at an almost exponential pace. From producing only blurry clips initially to now generating long videos with narrative structure, lighting consistency, and even style control, the industry appears to have reached a stage of relative maturity. However, if the evaluation criterion shifts from "whether a video can be generated" to "whether camera movement can be controlled," the issues become fully apparent. Most current models remain stuck in a quasi-2D generation paradigm—they excel at extending visual patterns over time but lack stable modeling of spatial structures. When perspective changes occur, these models often fail to maintain geometric consistency of the same object across frames: characters experience subtle but cumulative drift, architectural structures gradually distort during movement, and occlusion relationships struggle to remain continuous. This means the model does not generate a consistently observed world, but rather a series of visually similar yet spatially inconsistent results. Against this industry backdrop, the AGI Lab research team at Westlake University proposed the paper "Taming Video Models for 3D and 4D Generation via Zero Shot Camera Control," which notably was selected as a CVPR Highlight. Unlike previous approaches that introduced control capabilities by retraining models, this work reframes the problem at the inference stage itself, attempting to achieve camera control without altering model parameters.

On April 19, 2026, the second Beijing Yizhuang Humanoid Robot Half Marathon concluded successfully. Multiple "Linglong 2.0" humanoid robots equipped with the SpacemiT RISC-V AI CPU K3 chip completed the race. The "Linglong 2.0" is a humanoid robot platform developed by the Shanghai National and Local Co-built Humanoid Robot Innovation Center. In extreme scenarios involving long distances, high loads, and strong real-time demands, the K3 chip proved its capabilities through practical validation. Addressing the highly coupled system-level requirements of humanoid robot motion control—such as high-throughput AI inference, instant servo control response, power consumption constraints for extended endurance, and minimized transmission latency with multi-sensor parallelism—the K3 chip provides an integrated solution at the microarchitecture level. This marks that the RISC-V chip solution has achieved mature engineering capabilities to support high-dynamic, complex-environment humanoid robot competitions.

Architecture Advantage: Chip Microarchitecture Designed for Humanoid Robots  
Traditional multi-chip architectures like "CPU + MCU + NPU" rely on external bus bridges for inter-chip communication, leading to high latency uncertainty. In high-frequency servo scenarios exceeding 500Hz, microsecond-level jitter becomes an insurmountable systemic bottleneck. The K3 chip offers an integrated solution at the microarchitecture level:

excerpt_i18n.en:
Leiphone.com exclusively learned that former Huawei "Genius Youth" and Level 19 technical expert Zhao Lichen left the company in March 2026 to join Hangzhou Lagrange Embodied Technology Co., Ltd. Lagrange pursues a differentiated path from other embodied intelligence companies, focusing on the development of an embodied intelligence architecture (Agentic OS) and large-scale hardware deployment, aiming to establish an advantage in the most critical and challenging layer of embodied intelligence.  

01 Who is Zhao Lichen?  
According to public information, Zhao Lichen earned both his bachelor's and master's degrees in Software Engineering from Beihang University, with a long-term focus on 3D vision and multimodality. His related work has been cited over a thousand times, making him the only student from Beihang University selected for Huawei's "Genius Youth" program.  
During his undergraduate studies, he won the gold medal in the ACM-ICPC East Asia Regional Finals twice. In 2021, he participated in the pre-training of the INTERN 20B large model at SenseTime, making him one of the earliest practitioners of large-scale pre-training in China.  
As a rare master's graduate recruited through the "Genius Youth" program, Zhao Lichen joined Huawei in 2023 and built a team of over 20 people from scratch. He won second place in the Huawei Algorithm Competition and led the continuous iteration of the AI Smart Home Agent's end-cloud architecture. The related project won the China Telecom Excellence Innovation Award and is set for mass production in the second half of 2026.  
With his outstanding technical and delivery capabilities, Zhao Lichen entered the Level 19 promotion track within just over two years, becoming one of Huawei's youngest senior technical executives.

Según información pública, Zhao Lichen cursó sus estudios de grado y máster en Ingeniería de Software en la Universidad de Beihang, especializándose durante mucho tiempo en visión 3D y multimodalidad. Sus trabajos relacionados acumulan más de mil citas, y es el único estudiante de Beihang seleccionado hasta ahora para el programa de prodigios de Huawei.

excerpt_i18n.en: April 22, 2026 — SenseTime’s SenseAuto officially released Sage, an end-side multimodal agent base model. Sage adopts a MoE architecture with 32B total parameters and only 3B activated parameters, making it the industry’s first base model to achieve complex agent capabilities on the vehicle side. It leads global cloud-based models on PinchBench and has been deployed on NVIDIA Orin X edge platforms. AI has fully entered the agent era, but vehicle-side complex agent capabilities have relied on the cloud, while edge models, limited by computing power and parameters, could only handle simple command responses. Smart cockpits faced a dilemma: relying on the cloud introduced latency and high token costs, while sticking to the edge lacked true agent capabilities. Sage breaks this pattern, bringing cloud-level agent capabilities to the edge for the first time. As an edge agent base, Sage can integrate with mainstream agent frameworks like OpenClaw and Hermes, providing core support for more edge agent deployments across scenarios such as mobility and home. Sage’s strength has been validated in international public benchmarks. On the public agent benchmark PinchBench, Sage achieved a best task completion rate of 94%, surpassing Claude-Opus-4.6 (93.3%), Claude-Sonnet-4.6 (88.0%), and GPT-5.4 (90%).
excerpt_i18n.es: 22 de abril de 2026 — SenseTime Jueying lanza oficialmente el modelo base multimodal de agente en el extremo, Sage. Sage adopta la arquitectura MoE, con un total de 32B parámetros y solo 3B parámetros activos. Es el primer modelo base de la industria en lograr capacidades complejas de agente en el vehículo, con un rendimiento líder en PinchBench frente a los modelos en la nube globales de primer nivel, y ya se ha implementado en la plataforma de extremo NVIDIA Orin X. La IA ha entrado por completo en la era de los agentes, pero las capacidades complejas de agente en los vehículos dependen de la nube, mientras que los modelos en el extremo, limitados por la potencia de cálculo y los parámetros, solo pueden responder a instrucciones simples. El habitáculo inteligente se encuentra así en un dilema.
